newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to scrap selective credit controls.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to scrap selective credit controls.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Saturday it will scrap selective credit controls on land to boost the slowing economy, effective from September 1.

"The central bank, in order to avoid the long-term control affecting market function in money operations, and due to the slowing economy and sluggish real estate market, decides to scrap the seven-year-old selective credit controls, effective from September 1," the bank said in a statement.
In March 1989, the bank started various selective credit controls on land after money supply growth surged and real estate prices rocketed, the bank said.
During 1987 and 1989, speculation on land made real estate prices jump more than 300 percent in most major cities on the island.
The controls were designed to avoid money from flowing too much to land speculation, the statement said.
Because of economic situation changes, the bank has for seven times since 1989 gradually relaxed the selective credit controls, it said.
Currently, there remains only two controls on loans for land purchases and loans for golf course purchases, which will be fully scrapped from September 1, it said.
